question:
I'm trying to create a logic flow in my dbt codes basing on dates. The first attempt looks like this:

{% if '2024-01-17' == dateadd(day,-1,current_date()) %}

select current_date() as the_date

{% else %}

select dateadd(day,-1,current_date()) as the_date

{% endif %}

This failed to compile with the error saying current_date is not defined.

I tried to quote the function in the if block as below:

{% if '2024-01-17' == 'dateadd(day,-1,current_date())' %}

select current_date() as the_date

{% else %}

select dateadd(day,-1,current_date()) as the_date

{% endif %}

It compiled fine but it's because dbt treats 'dateadd(day,-1,current_date())' as a string, and it doesn't equal to '2024-01-17' so it executes the {% else %} block.

This question was posted on 2024-01-18 so dateadd(day,-1,current_date()) should be equal to '2024-01-17', so ideally the {% if %} block should be executed.

What should I change so that the {% if %} block is executed?

Thanks for your help.
title: Does dbt jinja's if block accept SQL functions when checking value?
answer:
To have yesterday date as a string in Jinja2, you can try the following:

{% set yesterday = (modules.datetime.datetime.now() - modules.datetime.timedelta(days=1)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d") %}

Hence, your code transforms to:

{% if '2024-01-17' == (modules.datetime.datetime.now() - modules.datetime.timedelta(days=1)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d") %}

select current_date() as the_date

{% else %}

select dateadd(day,-1,current_date()) as the_date

{% endif %}

However, it is best practice to keep logic out of your templating. Moreover, SQL allows us to do exactly what you want:

SELECT 
    CASE WHEN CURRENT_DATE() - 1 = DATE('2024-01-17')
        THEN CURRENT_DATE()
        ELSE DATEADD(DAY, -1, CURRENT_DATE())
    END AS the_date

If your date is a variable, you can also use it directly in your SQL code like this:

{% set date_check = '2024-01-17' %}
SELECT 
    CASE WHEN CURRENT_DATE() - 1 = DATE('{{ date_check }}')
        THEN CURRENT_DATE()
        ELSE DATEADD(DAY, -1, CURRENT_DATE())
    END AS the_date

I hope this helps!
